title: Subclass-Style Struct Composition (Subclass Coupling)
pattern: A composite struct deeply couples itself to an inner struct's implementation by acting as a pseudo-subclass, directly exposing and calling base methods internally.
why_bad: It mirrors the tightest form of object-oriented coupling. The "derived" struct is dependent on the entire private and public interface of the "base" struct. Changes in `BaseConnection` ripple downstream.
detection: Structs containing a standard wrapper field (often named `base` or `parent`) where the containing struct forwards or directly calls methods of the base in almost every method.
counterexample: Valid wrapper wrappers or adapters that implement standard traits (e.g., implementing `Read` by delegating to an inner `Read` type).
source: Eric Elliott, *Composing Software* (2019) ("Subclass Coupling"); Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Chapter 2 ("Inheritance").
